chapter: Queens Terrace, Decca records and Amen
title: Bob Carroll, Vernon King and John Brown
summary: Carroll's tenure, bassists King and Brown, and a 1940 photo.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: So it was Stovall and Courtney; Bob Carroll left you to go with Lucky Millinder at one point, around 1940; that's why he's not on the first record.
No, no, no. Bobby Carroll's on the first record.
He was with Lucky Millinder for a while; I know that because I have pictures of him with the band.
But he was on that, in
In 1940 he was with you, he was still with you.
I wish I had this list-- I got the list of my recordings. I've got it here, if you could stop that thing.
Vernon King was from St. Louis, I'm trying to think where you got him from, although he worked with Jeter&Pillars down in St. Louis.
I think he worked with Jeter&Pillars after.
I think before and also he was with (inaudible). I'm trying to think where you would have gotten him from; he must have been working with somebody.
I don't know, but anyway he was a good bass player.
But John Brown had also been with you before.
I had that little picture and I think maybe that was Barrell of Fun, or someplace, because Lloyd Phillips was on the picture and Bob Carroll is there, Willard Brown was there.
